goal: An autonomous trading research factory that continuously converts raw ideas into scored evidence across crypto, forex, and prediction markets.

plan.title: EMA Trend Gate on SOL - Volatility Edge Extension
plan.objective: Extend EMA Trend Gate strategy (0.528 OOS Sharpe on ETH with 1216 trades) to SOLUSDT. Hypothesis: SOL's higher volatility than ETH should generate more trade opportunities and potentially better risk-adjusted returns. Use 4h EMA regime filter + 1h RSI pullback entry logic that worked on ETH.
plan.hypothesis: SOL's higher volatility will produce more trade signals (exceeding ETH's 14.3 avg trades/window) with comparable or better risk-adjusted returns. If SOL underperforms ETH, it tests whether volatility alone is insufficient without underlying trend quality.
plan.strategy_rationale: The EMA Trend Gate strategy on ETH demonstrated 0.528 OOS Sharpe with high trade frequency (1216 total trades). This experiment tests whether the same strategy architecture generalizes to another volatile altcoin (SOL) or if ETH's results were asset-specific. SOL's higher volatility (typical daily range 3-5% vs ETH's 2-4%) should amplify RSI mean-reversion signals.
plan.instrument_selection_rule: Single instrument: SOL/USDT spot on Binance
dataset_requirements: Minimum 2 years of continuous 1h history (~17,520 bars)
Must include 2022-2023 bear market for regime diversity

historical_depth_requirement.justification: Crypto markets require multi-year history per policy to capture full market cycles. ETH experiment used 7.5 years (64,733 bars). SOL was listed on Binance in 2020, so ~2 years is available. Shorter than ETH but sufficient for SOL listing history.

source_plan.selection_reason: Binance is the primary source for SOLUSDT 1h data with full historical depth. The paginated fetcher can retrieve all available SOL history.

plan.scope_selection_rationale: SOL is the highest-volatility major altcoin in the portfolio, making it ideal for testing whether volatility-driven mean-reversion strategies generalize. SOL typically shows 30-50% higher ATR than ETH, providing a strong test of the volatility-as-signal-generator hypothesis.

data_acquisition.reason: Existing SOL data is insufficient: binance_solusdt_1h_1000.csv has only 1000 bars (~41 days), binance_solusdt_1h_live.csv has 500 bars (~20 days). Neither meets the 2-year minimum requirement.
commands: cd 'walk forward engine' && .venv/Scripts/python.exe -c "from data.fetchers.binance_paginated import BinancePaginatedFetcher; f = BinancePaginatedFetcher(); f.fetch_ohlcv('SOLUSDT', '1h', '2020-04-01', '2026-03-25', 'data/binance_solusdt_1h_deep.csv')"

implementation_steps: 1. Fetch full SOLUSDT 1h history from Binance using paginated fetcher
2. Verify data quality: check for gaps, validate OHLCV relationships
3. Create SOL-specific WFA config by copying ETH config and updating source_file
4. Run WFA with same param grid as ETH experiment (EMA periods pinned, RSI/hold_bars optimized)
5. Compare SOL results against ETH baseline metrics (0.528 Sharpe, 1216 trades, -16.37% DD)

evaluation_criteria.status_gate: WFA must complete with at least 30 OOS trades to be meaningful
evaluation_criteria.comparison_gate: SOL should generate >= 15 avg trades/window (exceeding ETH's 14.3) to validate volatility hypothesis

fallback_if_blocked: If SOL data fetch fails: Use limited SOL data (500 bars) with shorter WFA window (6 months training, 1 month testing)
If WFA fails: Debug with smoke test on 1000-bar subset
notes: ETH baseline: 0.528 OOS Sharpe, 1216 trades, -16.37% DD, 14.3 trades/window avg
SOL typically has 30-50% higher ATR than ETH - this is the primary variable being tested
The 4h EMA regime filter was noted as potentially too restrictive in prior ETH run - monitor if SOL performs worse due to reduced signal count
